title: Gold Insider Explains What China’s Gold Reserves Really Mean | Jeffrey Christian
speaker: Jeffrey Christian (CPM Group), interviewed by Ben Edelstein

macro_themes.view: PBOC monthly monetary gold figures are accurate; other state entities hold extra gold outside monetary reserves, and gold in China stays in China.
Reported deficits come from adding investment demand to fabrication demand; fundamentally the market is in surplus.
Much gold/silver information is bad and belief-driven; invest on knowledge, not beliefs.
He doesn't think the Fed funds rate has ever been correlated with gold prices.
Removing futures would not boost physical investment demand; leveraged speculators would just leave.

calls.reason: Has become more convinced gold belongs as a core portfolio holding; expects gold to outperform silver over the next decade; investment demand is the main price driver.
calls.quote: I think I've become much more convinced that gold makes sense as a core part of one's portfolio or wealth.

calls.condition: Relative view only: expects gold to outperform silver over the next decade.
calls.reason: Rejects the silver-deficit thesis: proper supply/demand shows surpluses absorbed by investor inventories, so deficit claims are not a reason to expect higher prices.
calls.quote: There's not a real silver deficit.

notes: Mostly an educational/myth-busting interview with no price levels or near-term calls. Date from listing (no date in transcript). Silver absolute bias not stated; only relative underperformance vs gold. Gold bullish long-term is implied from 'core part of portfolio' and gold>silver, low conviction.
